fact: The BDIC managing director says the Benue state government has launched a digital-skills programme to train 40,000 public servants across state and local governments in digital tools and e-governance platforms.
The BDIC managing director says over 4,800 Benue civil servants have been trained so far in ICT fundamentals, digital workflow systems and enterprise platforms, with weekly numbers rising.
Benue State announced it is committing to train 40,000 civil servants in digital tools and ICT skills, with the Nigerian Data Protection Commission providing part of the training.

fact: NITDA's director general says 54,377 civil servants have enrolled in the DL4ALL programme run with the Office of the Head of the Civil Service, and over 40 per cent have completed.
The Head of the Civil Service says DL4ALL ensures inclusive access to digital skills across ministries, departments and agencies.
NITDA's director general says the 54,377 civil servants enrolled in DL4ALL represent nearly 79 per cent participation, with over 40 per cent having completed.

Punch reports NITDA, with the Office of the Head of the Civil Service, has rolled out the Digital Literacy for All workforce programme on Cisco Networking Academy, with 45,813 to 54,377 learners enrolled per course.
Punch reports the DL4ALL programme reached the federal civil service across ministries, departments and agencies, with large ministries such as Education and Defence leading enrolments.
Punch reports DL4ALL enrolments cover an estimated 65 to 75 per cent of the federal civil service workforce, with completion of 38.1 to 44.6 per cent across the four modules.

The Office of the Head of the Civil Service says the DL4ALL programme with NITDA equips officers across MDAs with foundational digital skills, and honoured 35 officers from seven MDAs at its awards on 11 February 2026.
The Office of the Head of the Civil Service says the DL4ALL programme was designed to equip officers across MDAs with foundational digital skills.

NITDA says it launched a capacity-building programme for civil servants at the Office of the Head of the Civil Service, training champions from 43 MDAs on the DISCO learning platform for a Cisco-backed online course.
NITDA says the Head of the Civil Service stated all civil servants are required to complete the Cisco-backed online course within two months, with progress tracked across ministries.

The Federal Ministry of Information says the Head of the Civil Service launched on 10 September 2025 a Digital Literacy Action Plan, run with NITDA and Cisco on the National Digital Literacy Framework, that mandates participation by all officers in Core MDAs on a two-month timeline starting with ICT Directors and Digital Literacy Champions; no number trained is given.

The Head of the Civil Service launched the Nigeria Federal Civil Service Online Academy on 21 November 2024 as a beta platform offering civil servants online courses to upskill and reskill; no number trained is given.
